name: Sequoia & Kings Canyon National Parks
tagline: No trails, not even paved ones. But the forest next door says yes.
summary: Inside the parks, dogs are limited to campgrounds, picnic areas, parking lots and paved roads. Every trail is closed to them, including the paved paths to the General Sherman Tree, Big Trees and the General Grant Tree. The good news is twofold: the in-park lodges now take dogs, and the Sequoia National Forest that wraps around the parks allows leashed dogs on its trails, including giant sequoia groves of its own.
verdict: Bring your dog if you will camp or stay at a lodge and split your days between park drives and forest trails. Leave them home if you want to walk among the biggest trees in the park.

photo.alt: Giant sequoia trees on a hillside under a golden evening sky in Sequoia National Park
photo.author: Sasha Freemind

glance.note: Closed to dogs, including paved paths to General Sherman and General Grant
Pet rooms at Wuksachi, John Muir Lodge, Grant Grove Cabins and Cedar Grove, with a fee
Kaweah and Kings river banks inside campgrounds; Hume Lake in the national forest
6 ft or shorter, at all times
No pet fee. $35 per car entry, good for 7 days, covers both parks

allowed.name: Campgrounds
allowed.detail: Potwisha, Buckeye Flat, Lodgepole and Dorst Creek in Sequoia; Azalea, Sunset, Crystal Springs, Sentinel, Sheep Creek and Moraine in Kings Canyon. Leashed and never left alone.

allowed.name: Picnic areas and parking lots
allowed.detail: Hospital Rock, Lodgepole, Wolverton, Big Stump, Grant Grove and Cedar Grove picnic areas. The parking lot at the General Sherman Tree is fine; the path down to the tree is not.

allowed.name: Paved roads
allowed.detail: You can walk a dog along the shoulder of the Generals Highway, Kings Canyon Scenic Byway and campground roads. Watch for traffic on blind curves.

allowed.name: Pet rooms at the in-park lodges
allowed.detail: Wuksachi Lodge, John Muir Lodge, Grant Grove Cabins and Cedar Grove Lodge now offer dog rooms for a nightly pet fee with advance approval.

allowed.name: Sequoia National Forest trails (outside the parks)
allowed.detail: The national forest and Giant Sequoia National Monument surround both parks and allow leashed dogs on most trails, including Hume Lake and sequoia groves like Converse Basin.

allowed.name: Pet backpacks and strollers
allowed.detail: Allowed in developed areas only. They do not make a trail legal.

notAllowed.name: Every trail in both parks
notAllowed.detail: Including the paved General Sherman Tree Trail, Congress Trail, Big Trees Trail, General Grant Tree Trail, Moro Rock stairs, Crescent Meadow, Tokopah Falls and Zumwalt Meadow. Carried dogs count too.

notAllowed.name: Wilderness and backcountry
notAllowed.detail: No dogs on any backpacking route, including the High Sierra Trail and Rae Lakes Loop.

notAllowed.name: Shuttle buses
notAllowed.detail: The summer Sequoia shuttle does not carry pets.

notAllowed.name: Buildings
notAllowed.detail: Visitor centers, the Giant Forest Museum, markets and restaurants.

notAllowed.name: Crystal Cave
notAllowed.detail: No pets on the cave tour or the trail to it, and never leave a dog in the car at the trailhead.

notAllowed.name: Big Stump Basin and Grant Grove trails
notAllowed.detail: These are inside Kings Canyon National Park, so the park rule applies even though they sit right by the forest boundary.

hikes.name: Hume Lake Loop (Sequoia National Forest)
hikes.why: Flat lap around a mountain lake 10 miles from Grant Grove, outside the park boundary. Dogs on leash can swim at the shoreline. The one real dog hike within easy reach of the parks.
hikes.maps: Hume Lake Loop Trail, Hume Lake

hikes.name: Boole Tree Loop, Converse Basin Grove (Sequoia National Forest)
hikes.why: Reaches the Boole Tree, one of the biggest sequoias anywhere, on national forest land north of Grant Grove where leashed dogs are allowed. Rough dirt access road off Highway 180.

hikes.name: Trail of 100 Giants (Giant Sequoia National Monument)
hikes.why: Paved loop through a sequoia grove where leashed dogs are welcome. It is a long drive south of Three Rivers via Highway 190 and the Western Divide Highway, and sections were under repair in 2024; check the forest website before you go.
hikes.maps: Trail of 100 Giants, Long Meadow Grove

hangouts.name: Hospital Rock picnic area
hangouts.why: Low in the foothills near Potwisha, shaded, with the Middle Fork Kaweah close by. Warm in winter when the groves are under snow.

hangouts.name: Lodgepole Campground and the Marble Fork
hangouts.why: The river runs right through the campground. Dogs on leash can cool their paws at the edge in summer. The Tokopah Falls trail beyond is off limits.

hangouts.name: Cedar Grove picnic area and Sentinel Campground
hangouts.why: Deep in Kings Canyon beside the South Fork Kings River, with granite walls above. Open late spring to fall only.

hangouts.name: Grant Grove village lawn and parking
hangouts.why: You can see big sequoias from the road and the picnic area without stepping onto the closed Grant Tree Trail. Pet rooms at the lodge are steps away.

hangouts.name: Hume Lake (national forest)
hangouts.why: Sandy beach, lake swimming for dogs on leash, and a small store. The best full-day dog outing on a Kings Canyon trip.

rules: Keep your dog on a leash no longer than 6 feet, at all times.
Stay in campgrounds, picnic areas, parking lots and on paved roads. No trails, paved or not, and no carrying dogs onto them.
Never leave a dog unattended, at a campsite, tied up or in a vehicle.
Store dog food, bowls and treats in the bear locker at your site. Bears break into cars here.
Pick up waste and put it in a trash can or dumpster, not a bear locker.
Dogs cannot ride the summer shuttle bus.
Lodge pet rooms need advance approval and a nightly fee; dogs cannot be left alone in rooms.
Service dogs are allowed everywhere; emotional support animals follow the pet rules.

camping.name: Lodgepole Campground
camping.note: Biggest campground, by the Marble Fork Kaweah at 6,700 feet. Reserve on Recreation.gov; open spring to fall.

camping.name: Potwisha Campground
camping.note: Foothills near the Ash Mountain entrance at 2,100 feet, open year-round. Hot in summer, ideal in winter with a dog.

camping.name: Dorst Creek Campground
camping.note: Quieter, in the forest north of Lodgepole. Summer only.

camping.name: Azalea and Sunset Campgrounds, Grant Grove
camping.note: Walking distance to Grant Grove village. Azalea stays open in winter, first come first served off season.

camping.name: Sentinel and Sheep Creek, Cedar Grove
camping.note: Down in Kings Canyon beside the river. Open roughly May to October when the road is open.

lodging.name: Wuksachi Lodge, Sequoia
lodging.note: Limited pet rooms, up to 2 dogs, $25 per pet per night. Book early and ask for a pet room.

lodging.name: John Muir Lodge and Grant Grove Cabins, Kings Canyon
lodging.note: Pet-friendly rooms with a $25 nightly fee per pet and prior approval. Cedar Grove Lodge is listed as dog-friendly too.

lodging.name: Lazy J Ranch Motel, Three Rivers
lodging.note: Dog-friendly motel 6 miles from the Ash Mountain entrance. Per-pet fee; reports on the amount differ.

lodging.name: Sequoia Riverfront Cabins and Gateway Lodge, Three Rivers
lodging.note: Cabins on the Kaweah River with a pet fee per night.

lodging.name: Comfort Inn & Suites Sequoia Kings Canyon, Three Rivers
lodging.note: Up to 2 dogs with a nightly fee and a weight limit. Sources disagree on the limit, so check.

seasons.title: Winter (December to March)
seasons.detail: Chains are often required on the Generals Highway, and the road between the two parks can close. Potwisha and Azalea stay open; snow-covered roads are not open to dogs on foot.

seasons.title: Summer crowds and heat
seasons.detail: Three Rivers and the foothills top 100 F in July and August. Base at Lodgepole or Grant Grove where it is 20 degrees cooler, and walk early.

seasons.title: Kings Canyon Scenic Byway
seasons.detail: The road into Cedar Grove opens around late April and closes in November. Hume Lake is reachable most of the year.

seasons.title: Fire and smoke
seasons.detail: Late summer wildfire smoke can make exercise hard on dogs. Check air quality and park alerts before you drive up.

wildlife: Black bears are everywhere. Keep dog food and bowls in the bear locker and never in the car or tent.
Mountain lions live in the foothills and canyons. Keep dogs close at dawn and dusk and do not let them run ahead.
Rattlesnakes are common below 6,000 feet around Potwisha, Hospital Rock and Cedar Grove in warm months.
Ticks and foxtails fill the foothill grass from spring into summer. Check paws, ears and armpits after every walk.
checklist: Water and a bowl; campground taps can be far from your site
A 6-foot leash, not a retractable one
Tire chains in winter; the park requires them on short notice
A tick remover and a comb for foxtails
Waste bags and a way to carry them to a dumpster
A crate or blanket for lodge rooms; dogs cannot be left alone
Vaccine records in case you need a vet in Three Rivers or Visalia
